reports.title: Impact of Acute Aerobic Exercise on Genome-Wide DNA-Methylation in Natural Killer Cells—A Pilot Study
reports.authors: Schenk A; Koliamitra C; Bauer CJ; Schier R; Schweiger MR; Bloch W; Zimmer P
reports.version_date: Received 5 April 2019; Accepted 16 May 2019; Published 19 May 2019 (p.1)
reports.inclusion_reason: Single identifiable acute bout (incremental cycle-ergometer test to volitional exhaustion); pre-exercise baseline (t0) and immediate post-cessation sample (t1, 1 min) with immune-linked direct measures (sorted NK-cell genome-wide DNA methylation; NK-cell subset % by flow cytometry); adults (mean age 61.4±8.0y) (p.3 §2, §2.1-2.2).
reports.reviewer_notes: AI stand-in reviewer B opinion only; not a human screening decision. Core A rationale: identifiable single bout + pre/post sampling + immune-linked direct cellular/omics measures (contract 2.1-2.2). No population, infection or treatment-cohort flags apply.
reports.author_stated_use: Exploratory/mechanistic: 'to generate first insights into the influence of a single bout of exercise on genome-wide DNA-methylation in isolated NK-cells...to open the field for such analyses' (Abstract, p.1); framed as hypothesis-generating pilot, not a monitoring/diagnostic tool.
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.7-8 §4.1-4.2: authors attribute methylation changes to direct NK-cell epigenetic adaptation and explicitly argue the change is 'not driven by changes in NK-cell subsets' (redistribution); term 'open window' is not used anywhere in the text; no immunosuppression/susceptibility claim is made about this acute result.

study_families.study_label: Schenk 2019 NK-cell genome-wide methylation acute-exercise pilot (single-group pre/post)
study_families.design: Single-group pre-post acute-exercise challenge; no randomization, no control arm, no training intervention (p.3 §2).
study_families.training_load: NR (habitual training status of participants not reported)
study_families.study_notes: Ethics: Declaration of Helsinki; approved by University Hospital of Cologne ethics committee (IRB#13-274), written informed consent (p.3 §2). No external funding (Funding statement, p.8).

cohorts.cohort_label: Five healthy women recruited by regional newspaper announcement, Cologne, Germany (Dec 2014-Sept 2015)
cohorts.baseline_health: 'Healthy' defined as no acute or chronic disease; any drug intake was an exclusion criterion (p.3 §2).
cohorts.sport: NA (general incremental cycle-ergometer fitness test, not a specific sport)
cohorts.cohort_notes: Participants' characteristics (Table 1, p.4): weight 60.2±4.0 kg, height 166.2±4.1 cm, BMI 20.0±1.5 kg/m2, waist 84.2±5.5 cm, max power 165.0±13.7 W, VO2peak 32.4±3.8 mL/min/kg.
cohorts.age_range: Mean 61.4 ± 8.0 years (Table 1, p.4); explicit min-max age range not reported (NR for range specifically).

report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: All 5 recruited women analyzed for both the NK-cell methylation endpoint and the PBMC flow-cytometry subset-control endpoint (p.3-4).
report_cohort_links.link_notes: Single report, single cohort, single bout; no sub-studies.

analyte_id.standard_name: NK-cell genome-wide DNA methylation assay universe

measurements.platform: Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip; Genome Studio 2011.1 methylation module (p.3 §2.4)
measurements.cell_context: Sorted NK cells (CD3-CD56+, negative magnetic selection from PBMC)
measurements.comparison: Within-subject paired: before (t0) vs 1 min after (t1) acute incremental cycle exercise, n=5 (p.3 §2.7)
measurements.missing_data: 1,304/865,918 probes (0.2%) failed detection p≤0.05 filter and were excluded (p.4 §3.2).
measurements.tested_universe_unit: CpG probes (detected, passed per-sample detection p≤0.05 filter)
measurements.tested_universe: Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip probes passing detection p≤0.05 in ≥90% of samples (p.3 §2.7, p.4 §3.2).

analyte_id.standard_name: Genome-wide differential DNA methylation signature, NK cells, acute exercise

measurements.platform: Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChip; Genome Studio 2011.1 methylation module
measurements.comparison: Within-subject paired: before (t0) vs 1 min after (t1), n=5
measurements.effect_measure: FDR-corrected DiffScore (Illumina custom differential model, transformation of p-value; DiffScore>=|13| ~ p<=0.05, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR) (p.3 §2.7)
measurements.effect_value: 33/864,614 detected targets changed (0.004%); 19 targets (57.6%) decreased methylation, 14 targets (42.4%) increased; delta-beta range -0.16 to +0.18; 25/33 targets annotated to a gene (10 in gene body, 8 unannotated) (p.4 §3.2, Table 2 p.5).
measurements.multiplicity: FDR correction via Illumina GenomeStudio custom differential model (Benjamini-Hochberg); probes with detection p>0.05 in >10% of samples excluded pre-analysis (p.3 §2.7).
measurements.donor_level_inference: n=5 paired donors; each donor contributes one pre and one post sorted-NK-cell sample; no pooling reported.
measurements.missing_data: 1,304/865,918 probes (0.2%) excluded by detection-p filter before differential analysis (p.4 §3.2).
measurements.null_findings: Implicit: 864,581/864,614 detected targets (99.996%) did not meet the DiffScore>=|13| threshold; full non-significant list not individually reported (p.4 §3.2).
measurements.measurement_notes: Gene Ontology/DAVID functional annotation (Table 3, p.6) is bioinformatic annotation of the 25 genes, not measured immune function (GO/pathway outputs are annotation/hypothesis per manual, not functional assay).
measurements.candidate_in_original_aims_methods: No prespecified immune-gene candidate panel; study aim was exploratory genome-wide screening ('to generate first insights...to open the field', Abstract p.1); the 33 targets/25 genes are post-hoc statistically thresholded hits, not an aims/methods-defined immune-candidate list.

measurements.comparison: Within-subject paired: before (t0) vs 1 min after (t1), n=5
measurements.measurement_notes: FASLG singled out in Discussion as the gene with the most DAVID functional annotations (Table 3) and as a candidate NK-cytotoxicity mechanism gene (FAS-ligand, apoptosis induction). Authors note FASLG gene expression in leukocytes was previously reported unchanged immediately post-exercise but increased 3h later (citing Mooren 2004, ref 23 - NOT measured in this study). FASLG gene expression itself was not measured here (p.7 §4.1).
measurements.candidate_in_original_aims_methods: No; FASLG emerged post-hoc as the top DAVID-annotated gene among the 25 differentially methylated genes, not a prespecified candidate.

measurements.platform: Flow cytometry (BD FACS Array; anti-CD3 APC-C7, anti-CD56 PE) (p.3 §2.6)
measurements.cell_context: PBMC gated CD3- CD56+ (NK cells); CD56bright and CD56dim subsets as % of NK-cell pool.
measurements.comparison: Within-subject paired: before (t0) vs 1 min after (t1), n=5, Wilcoxon signed-rank test
measurements.effect_measure: % of NK-cell pool; Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value
measurements.effect_uncertainty: p=0.080 for both comparisons (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p.4 §3.4).
measurements.multiplicity: NR (no multiplicity correction reported for this single comparison pair).
measurements.null_findings: Yes - both changes explicitly reported as not statistically significant (p=0.080, p=0.080) (p.4 §3.4).
measurements.measurement_notes: Used by authors as an internal control: absence of significant subset redistribution supports their argument that the genome-wide methylation changes (M-R03-002) are not driven by compositional shift between CD56bright/CD56dim subsets (p.7-8 §4.2).
measurements.candidate_in_original_aims_methods: Yes - flow-cytometry control of NK-cell subset distribution explicitly planned as methodology (§2.6, p.3) to control for compositional confounding of the methylation result.

precision_validation.evidence_notes: Platform described as 'robust and reliable', citing external validation (Pidsley et al. 2016, ref 26) and FDR/detection-p QC filtering was applied (864,614/865,918 probes passed), but no within-study technical replicate, ICC or CV for this NK-cell methylation assay itself is reported (p.8 §4.3).

Two timepoints only: pre-exercise baseline and 1 min post-cessation (time_bin 0_to_lt30min, within_window); no samples beyond 1 min, no outside-window (>72h) recovery sample; authors note 'more measurement time points could give information about the kinetics' (p.8 §4.3).

Sorted CD3-CD56+ NK cells used specifically to avoid PBMC-conglomerate confounding (cell-type-specific design is the paper's central methodological contribution, Intro p.2, Discussion §4.1 p.7); co-measured with flow-cytometry subset data (M-R03-004) without a formal statistical association test between the two readouts.
Single pre-post pair per participant (n=5); no repeated baseline, no repeat bout, no ICC/CV/responder analysis; cannot establish individualized or reproducible methylation profile.

Gene-level functional annotation via DAVID/GO (Table 3) only; no measured NK-cell cytotoxicity, degranulation or other direct function assay; authors state 'whether or not these changes lead to functional adaptions needs to be elucidated' (Abstract) and gene expression of the affected genes was not measured (p.8 §4.3).

n=5 single-centre pilot explicitly framed as hypothesis-generating ('to open the field', Abstract); no independent cohort or participant-split validation; data openly deposited (GEO GSE129376) enabling future reanalysis but this is not itself validation.

Requires venous draw, density-gradient PBMC isolation, magnetic-bead NK sorting, column DNA extraction and EPIC array processing; authors flag NK-subpopulation DNA yield as a 'bottle neck' for further fractionation (p.8 §4.3); no cost/turnaround/field-use data reported.
Standard commercial antibody panel (anti-CD3 APC-C7, anti-CD56 PE) and defined gating (CD3-CD56+; CD56bright/dim) described (p.3 §2.6), but no replicate/CV/ICC reported for the flow assay.
Same two timepoints as the methylation assay (pre-exercise baseline; 1 min post-cessation, bin 0_to_lt30min, within_window).
Direct immune-cell subset proportions (NK CD56bright vs CD56dim), a conventional direct immune index (marker_family NK_count_or_cytotoxicity).
n=5, single pre/post pair; no repeated measurement or individual threshold/responder analysis.
No functional (e.g., cytotoxicity) or clinical endpoint examined for this subset measure; used only as an internal compositional-confounding check for the methylation result (p.7-8 §4.2).
Not examined; this measure's only role in the paper is as an internal QC/confound-exclusion check, not a validated or externally tested marker in its own right.
Not discussed by authors; flow cytometry is a routine assay but no cost/turnaround/field-use statement is given in this report.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Single identifiable acute bout (incremental cycle-ergometer test to volitional exhaustion) with a pre-exercise baseline (t0) and an immediate post-cessation sample (t1, 1 min; within the 0-72h organising window, bin 0_to_lt30min), plus immune-linked direct measures (sorted NK-cell genome-wide DNA methylation; NK-cell subset flow cytometry) in adults (p.3 §2, §2.1-2.2, Table 1). No infection outcome, training intervention or population boundary issue applies; this satisfies Core A per contract 2.1-2.2 regardless of the very short (~15 min) bout duration or small n=5, since the review sets no exposure threshold.

unresolved_questions: older_adult_subgroup: mean age is 61.4+/-8.0y (clearly 'older' by common usage) but the authors never use an 'older adult' label or threshold; the dictionary ties this field to author-defined framing ('as defined by the original authors'), so I left it NR rather than inferring older_adult_cohort from age alone. Unclear whether reviewers should infer this field from age when authors are silent.

Candidate-universe mismatch: the manual's rule to enumerate 'all named immune candidates from original aims/methods regardless of significance' assumes a hypothesis-driven gene panel. This study is a hypothesis-free genome-wide screen (865,918 probes) reporting only the 33 CpGs/25 genes that passed a post-hoc statistical threshold (DiffScore>=|13|); there is no prespecified candidate list and no full null-result table. I charted one assay_universe_summary row plus an aggregate reported_result_summary row (plus one singled-out gene, FASLG) rather than 25 separate per-gene rows. Unclear whether the manual intends per-target/per-gene rows for this kind of exploratory array study, and whether my 4-row simplification under-serves the 'preserve full candidate universe' rule.

age_range field: only mean+/-SD (61.4+/-8.0y) is reported, no explicit min-max range, even though the field description example is 'X-Y y; mean...'. I recorded the mean/SD with a note rather than NR; unclear if that is the intended handling when a dispersion statistic but no literal range is given.

exercise_duration: the ~15 min bout duration appears only in the Discussion (§4.2), not in Methods, and is described as approximate for the group rather than per-participant. Unclear whether a Discussion-only approximate value should be flagged UNCLEAR/NR instead of recorded as-is with a locator caveat.
